picks.name: BAE BAE
picks.bio: Kumi James, DJ/producer/activist from Los Angeles, runs the Hood Rave party series. "gauze" (July 24, 2026) is her debut EP for Planet Mu.
picks.why_listen: Percussion-centered EP moving through dissonant garage, footwork and jungle, built around real recordings from Gaza -- grief and urgency rendered as rhythm rather than just a message. Heavy, purposeful, still functional for a floor.

picks.name: Speaker Music
picks.source_note: Planet Mu roster mate of BAE BAE (above).
picks.bio: DeForrest Brown Jr.'s project, closing out a Planet Mu partnership that started in 2019. "Synoptic Audio" (July 10, 2026) is billed as his final album for the label.
picks.why_listen: Live electronic improvisation -- dense drone, played keyboards and drums, somewhere between free jazz and techno. Not a peak-time tool, but a strong one for a set that wants to slow down and think for a minute.

picks.name: Dengue Dengue Dengue
picks.source_note: Already seeded (Peru duo behind Kebrada, previously featured for their N.A.A.F.I-era work).
picks.bio: Lima duo Felipe Salmon and Rafael Pereira, running their own label Kebrada. "Abisal" (Aug 6, 2026) is a 6-track collaborative album with Prisma, released under the DNGDNGDNG name.
picks.why_listen: Six days old. A survey of "the depths" -- chemical/geological/organic textures over their usual percussion-forward electronic base. One track, "Ripio," features Jaijiu.

picks.name: Kush Jones
picks.source_note: Similar scene to BAE BAE -- jungle/footwork, Juke Bounce Werk collective. Also already in your library (Bass/House playlists) -- good cross-check on this connection.
picks.bio: Bronx producer, member of the international Juke Bounce Werk collective alongside DJ Swisha, DJ Noir, and Jae Drago. "Building" (March 27, 2026) is a 3-track self-released EP.
picks.why_listen: Jungle/footwork fusion from someone who mostly self-releases -- "Tekno Track" (feat. Kanyon) is the one to start with if you want a quick read on the EP.

picks.name: Nuevos Rios
picks.bio: Collaboration between Colombia's Canalón de Timbiquí (led by Nidia Góngora, also known from Quantic/Ondatrópica/The Bongo Hop) and Toulouse trio Reco Reco. Self-titled album "Nuevos Rios" (March 27, 2026) is on ZZK Records.
picks.why_listen: Marimba, percussion and voice from Afro-Colombian tradition interlaced with keyboards, guitar and drums -- a hypnotic bridge between West Africa, the Caribbean, and club electronics. Good change-of-pace record, not a straight club tool.
